title: ICMR Guidelines for Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in India

chunks.topic: Glycemic Targets, First-line Pharmacotherapy, and Hypoglycemia Management
chunks.content: Metformin (500mg-1000mg with or after meals to minimize gastrointestinal discomfort) remains the standard initial pharmacotherapy for Type 2 Diabetes alongside individualized medical nutrition therapy. General glycemic target is HbA1c < 7.0%, fasting blood glucose 80-130 mg/dL, and postprandial glucose < 180 mg/dL. In patients on sulfonylureas (e.g. Glimepiride) or Insulin, recognition of hypoglycemia (blood glucose < 70 mg/dL, manifesting with shakiness, cold sweating, tachycardia, dizziness, or confusion) is essential. The Rule of 15 must be applied: consume 15g fast-acting carbohydrate (3-4 glucose tablets or 1/2 cup fruit juice), wait 15 minutes, and re-test.
chunks.contraindications: Metformin is contraindicated in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2), acute metabolic acidosis, severe hypoxemia, or acute hepatic failure due to lactic acidosis risk.
chunks.warnings: Symptoms of diabetic ketoacidosis (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, acetone fruity breath, deep rapid breathing) or severe hyperosmolar state require urgent inpatient hospitalization.
chunks.home_care: Daily inspection of feet for blisters, cuts, or redness; wearing comfortable non-binding footwear; consuming complex carbohydrates rich in fiber (oats, millets, barley) and eliminating refined sugary beverages and sweets.
chunks.citation: ICMR Guidelines for Management of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2024 Edition), Chapter 5: Pharmacological Management, pp. 44-58.
